(I am a student of PearlV's.)

Please could you tell me :

How does one grain of silver halide reflect/absorb different amounts of light depending on angle?

Are the grains of silver halide made of several particles or just one?

Are the grains of silver halide 3 dimensional, or flat?

The only way I can visualise an individual grain reflecting differently depending on angle is if its 3D/ not flat. I was wondering if they were semi-spheres with the convex side facing you. This way different sides of the grain could reflect differently. I then thought, because the viewing angle is greater on one plane than another, that maybe the grains were more like semi-egg shaped, or elongated semi-sphere's, again with convex side facing viewer.

This made me think that if they were elongated they would need to be allinged in the same direction. But this all falls apart if the grain reacts as a whole, whereas if the grain was made of several particles then certain particles within one grain could be tarnished by different amounts, and therefore reflect differently at different angles.

Am I miles off?

Many thanks for any information/clarification.

(I'm losing sleep )
